clue.text: Extremely zany type of art and dance music

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities of the following word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the two end letters of zany
Art Deco is a style of design and art

explanation.surface: A description of some wild style of painting and music to dance to.
explanation.definitionFit: Zydeco is a Louisiana Creole genre played with accordion and washboard, made for dancing.

clue.text: Legal workers born outside the period 21 March to 19 April?

parts.note: born outside a span of dates means not born within it
the star sign covering those dates

explanation.surface: Seems to describe lawyers defined oddly by their birthdays.
explanation.walkthrough: Anyone born outside those dates is NOT ARIES, which runs together as NOTARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Notaries are public officials who witness signatures and certify documents, a branch of the legal profession.

clue.text: Turn down official employment

parts.note: a referee is a match official
employment in the sense of putting something to use

explanation.surface: Someone rejecting an official job offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse an offer is to decline it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Meandering answer upset the top guy

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read bottom to top

parts.note: the monarch is the man at the top

explanation.surface: A rambling reply that offended the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Answer' abbreviates to the usual three letters used in exam marking; 'upset' only works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A river snaking across a plain winds back and forth, exactly as one meandering does.

clue.text: Suggest that, cryptically?

parts.note: surface reading: imply something in a roundabout way
setter's reading: the word that is built as the eighth letter placed in a word for tit-for-tat

explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, HINT AT splits as H IN TAT, and putting H inside TAT spells THAT, the word in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something is to suggest it indirectly, the meaning carried by the verb phrase.

clue.text: Chemist quick to hide damage

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one word wraps round the other

explanation.surface: A pharmacist in a hurry to cover up some harm done.
explanation.walkthrough: Chemist is the British word for a drugstore, so the definition names the shop, not the person.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a chemist's shop is where prescriptions are dispensed, i.e. a pharmacy.

clue.text: Embargoes involving dodgy money? Certainly not!

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound, so these letters are jumbled
involving means taking in, so one word wraps round the other

explanation.surface: Someone flatly refusing to accept sanctions tainted by shady finance.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled money goes between B and ANS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal or denial, an idiom meaning not at all.

clue.text: Sound location for seeing things

definitions.note: sight is the faculty used for seeing things

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how a word is spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: a site is a location; the target is spelt differently but said the same

explanation.surface: Reads like advice on a good spot for viewing, or hints at hallucination.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is the sense or faculty of vision, which is what lets people see things.

clue.text: In retirement, a wonderful person resists huge amounts of cash

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: a gem is a wonderful person
to buck a trend is to resist it

explanation.surface: A retired saint who turns down fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: A GEM reversed is MEGA, then BUCKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Megabucks is slang for very large sums of money, a fortune.

clue.text: Singular right-wing newspaper article

parts.note: Tory is the British name for a Conservative

explanation.surface: An odd piece printed in a conservative paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists call each news report or feature a story.

clue.text: Nothing good about scary character

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Remarks that there is nothing good to say of a frightening figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folk tales, a frightening figure.

clue.text: Rookie's lack of depravity?

parts.note: a lack of something means there is none of it

explanation.surface: Suggests a newcomer is innocent of wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a beginner, just as a rookie is a first-year recruit or newcomer.

clue.text: Drink almost beginning to taste better

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word is just its opening letter

parts.note: to cap a story is to better it

explanation.surface: A drink that very nearly starts tasting better.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is an alcoholic drink taken just before going to bed.

clue.text: Messenger job accepted by mailmen periodically

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so it goes inside the other piece
periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: a post is a position of employment

explanation.surface: A courier given a job by the postal workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' keeps the even-numbered letters, not the odd ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostle comes from the Greek for one sent out, a messenger, as Christ's twelve disciples were sent to preach.

clue.text: Smoked meat to stuff inside fresh pitas

indicators.note: fresh suggests remade, so these letters are reworked
inside places one word within the other

parts.note: to ram is to cram or stuff

explanation.surface: Instructions for filling flatbreads with cured meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned beef that has been brined, spiced and smoked, a deli staple.

clue.text: Was dishonest and continued being heartless

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is removed

parts.note: to go on existing is to have lived

explanation.surface: Someone who kept up a lie for life.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVED loses its middle V to give LIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Lied is the past tense of lie, to tell untruths, so it means was dishonest.

clue.text: Crown dependency is tops!

parts.note: Jersey is a Channel Island, a British Crown dependency

explanation.surface: A cheer that an island under the Crown is the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tops' reads as praise; it is the plural noun for upper garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerseys are knitted pullovers or sports shirts, garments worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Scattered crop said to need regenerating

indicators.note: regenerating means rebuilding anew, so the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A patchy harvest reportedly needs to be renewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' looks like a sound signal but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring irregularly here and there, so scattered in time or place.

clue.text: Leads from computer equipment in case with a keyboard

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters

parts.note: first letters of the two words
taken as written; with just joins

explanation.surface: Cables from computer kit in a housing with a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The celesta is a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal bars, famous in the Sugar Plum Fairy dance.

clue.text: Sort of sweatier pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of rather sweatier trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a noun for trousers or a verb for gasping; it is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase as it were qualifies a word as loosely used, much like saying so to speak.

clue.text: Tennessee introduces state bar

indicators.note: to introduce is to bring in, so one word goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A Tennessee bill banning something in the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like it should be another US state alongside Tennessee; here it is a verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or public house where drinks are served across a counter.

clue.text: Careless agent takes on large operation

indicators.note: to take on is to take in, so the spy word holds the others

parts.note: short form, as in a military op

explanation.surface: A slapdash spy taking on a big mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy work is slapdash, done without due care or attention to detail.

clue.text: Somewhat grotesque, alarming scream

indicators.note: somewhat means a part of, so the answer is a piece of the following words

parts.note: letters spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A rather grotesque and frightening shriek.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeal is a high-pitched cry, a shrill sort of scream.

clue.text: Fertiliser remains underneath garden container

indicators.note: in a down clue, underneath places one piece below the other in the grid

explanation.surface: Ashes put at the bottom of a garden pot to feed plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium compound used widely to fertilise soil.

clue.text: Dignified government party

parts.note: a rave is a lively dance party

explanation.surface: A solemn, stately reception held by the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave as an adjective means serious and solemn in manner, which is dignified.

clue.text: Architectural design partner ultimately implicated in terrible tax abuse

indicators.note: implicated in means caught up within, so the letter goes among the others
terrible suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled
ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A design partner caught up in a nasty tax scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: R joins TAX ABUSE and all nine letters are rearranged into BEAUX ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaux Arts names the ornate classical style of architecture taught at the Paris École des Beaux-Arts.

clue.text: Computer-controlled electric vehicles put in reverse

indicators.note: reverse means going backwards, so the word is read from the end

explanation.surface: Self-driving electric cars being backed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart describes devices with built-in processors, such as a smart meter or phone.

clue.text: Most regular tastes die out

indicators.note: out suggests disorder or being put wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The habits we keep longest are the tastes that fade away.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadiest means most even and unvarying, so most regular in rhythm or habit.
